decisions.reason: The terms note: prophets speak to kings in 합쇼체 unless the scene sets otherwise; the king, who has just called him "my father", is still the king.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לְמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַרְכֵּ֤ב יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־הַקֶּ֔שֶׁת וַיַּרְכֵּ֖ב יָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֧שֶׂם אֱלִישָׁ֛ע יָדָ֖יו עַל־יְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to [the] king of Israel, Make ride your hand on the bow; and he made ride his hand, and put Elisha his hands on [the] hands of the king.

en.L: And he said to the king of Israel, "Make your hand ride on the bow." And he made his hand ride [on it], and Elisha put his hands on the hands of the king.
en.B: Then he said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand to the bow." He did so, and Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands.
en.R: Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Take hold of the bow." When he had done this, Elisha put his own hands on the king's hands.

es.L: Y dijo al rey de Israel: «Haz cabalgar tu mano sobre el arco». E hizo cabalgar su mano [sobre él], y Eliseo puso sus manos sobre las manos del rey.
es.B: Luego le dijo al rey de Israel: «Pon tu mano en el arco». Él lo hizo, y Eliseo puso sus manos sobre las del rey.
es.R: Luego Eliseo le dijo al rey de Israel: «Agarra el arco». Cuando lo hizo, Eliseo puso sus propias manos sobre las manos del rey.

fr.L: Et il dit au roi d’Israël : « Fais monter ta main sur l’arc. » Et il fit monter sa main [dessus], et Élisée mit ses mains sur les mains du roi.
fr.B: Puis il dit au roi d’Israël : « Mets ta main sur l’arc. » Le roi le fit, et Élisée posa ses mains sur les mains du roi.
fr.R: Ensuite Élisée a dit au roi d’Israël : « Tiens l’arc en main. » Quand le roi l’a fait, Élisée a posé ses propres mains sur celles du roi.

sw.L: Naye akamwambia mfalme wa Israeli, "Ipandishe mkono wako juu ya upinde." Naye akaupandisha mkono wake [juu yake], na Elisha akaweka mikono yake juu ya mikono ya mfalme.
sw.B: Kisha akamwambia mfalme wa Israeli, "Weka mkono wako kwenye upinde." Akafanya hivyo, na Elisha akaweka mikono yake juu ya mikono ya mfalme.
sw.R: Kisha Elisha akamwambia mfalme wa Israeli, "Shika upinde." Alipokwisha kufanya hivyo, Elisha akaweka mikono yake mwenyewe juu ya mikono ya mfalme.

vi.L: Ông nói với vua Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Hãy đặt tay vua trên cây cung." Vua đặt tay [trên đó], và Ê-li-sê đặt tay mình trên tay vua.
vi.B: Rồi ông nói với vua Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Xin vua cầm lấy cây cung." Vua làm theo, và Ê-li-sê đặt tay mình trên tay vua.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-li-sê nói với vua Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Xin vua cầm cây cung lên." Khi vua đã làm vậy, Ê-li-sê đặt tay mình lên tay vua.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 이스라엘 왕에게 말했다. "당신의 손을 활 위에 올리십시오." 그리고 그가 [그 위에] 손을 올렸다. 그리고 엘리사가 자기 손을 왕의 손 위에 얹었다.
ko.B: 그리고 그가 이스라엘 왕에게 말했다. "활을 손에 잡으십시오." 왕이 그렇게 하자, 엘리사가 자기 손을 왕의 손 위에 얹었다.
ko.R: 엘리사가 이스라엘 왕에게 말했다. "활을 잡으십시오." 왕이 활을 잡자, 엘리사가 자기 손을 왕의 손 위에 얹었다.

decisions.choice: make your hand ride on the bow: take the bow in hand, ready to draw
decisions.reason: The verb means to set something on top of something else, as a rider on a horse. Here it means gripping the bow to shoot.

decisions.choice: Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands: the strength for the shot comes through the prophet
decisions.reason: The prophet's hands over the king's show that the victory the arrow stands for is Yahweh's gift through his word, not the king's own power (verse 17, "the LORD's arrow").

decisions.choice: put your hand to / take hold of; He did so
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture (m1) and do not repeat the whole phrase in the narrative.

decisions.choice: "Haz cabalgar tu mano" (L); "Pon tu mano en el arco" (B); "Agarra el arco" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the hand riding on the bow; Balanced and Readable give its sense, as the English does (m1).

decisions.choice: "Fais monter ta main sur l'arc"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "make ride"; "faire monter" keeps the picture of the hand mounting the bow while staying French (m1).

decisions.choice: Ipandishe mkono wako juu ya upinde
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of making the hand "ride" on the bow with "kupandisha"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: đặt tay vua trên cây cung (L)
alternatives: cho tay vua cưỡi trên cây cung
decisions.reason: "Make your hand ride" cannot be kept word for word in Vietnamese; Literal says "put your hand on the bow", which keeps the picture of the hand resting on it.

decisions.choice: "당신의 손" when Elisha speaks to the king
decisions.reason: A prophet speaks as Yahweh's messenger, not as a subject; Literal keeps the possessive with "당신", and Balanced and Readable leave it out, as Korean usually does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּתַ֧ח הַחַלּ֛וֹן קֵ֖דְמָה וַיִּפְתָּ֑ח וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֤ע יְרֵה֙ וַיּ֔וֹר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חֵץ־תְּשׁוּעָ֤ה לַֽיהוָה֙ וְחֵ֣ץ תְּשׁוּעָ֣ה בַֽאֲרָ֔ם וְהִכִּיתָ֧ אֶת־אֲרָ֛ם בַּאֲפֵ֖ק עַד־כַּלֵּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Open the window eastward; and he opened. And said Elisha, Shoot; and he shot. And he said, An arrow of victory for Yahweh, and an arrow of victory over Aram; and you will strike Aram in Aphek until finishing.

en.L: And he said, "Open the window eastward." And he opened [it]. And Elisha said, "Shoot." And he shot. And he said, "An arrow of victory for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and an arrow of victory over Aram! And you will strike Aram in Aphek until making an end."
en.B: He said, "Open the window toward the east," and he opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" and he shot. Then Elisha said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You will strike down Aram at Aphek until you have made an end of it."
en.R: "Open the east window," Elisha said, and the king opened it. "Shoot!" Elisha said, and the king shot. Then Elisha said, "This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s arrow of victory, the arrow that means victory over Aram! You will defeat the Arameans at Aphek until you have wiped them out."

es.L: Y dijo: «Abre la ventana hacia el oriente». Y [la] abrió. Y Eliseo dijo: «Dispara». Y disparó. Y dijo: «¡Flecha de victoria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y flecha de victoria sobre Aram! Y herirás a Aram en Afec hasta acabar».
es.B: Le dijo: «Abre la ventana que da al oriente», y él la abrió. Eliseo le dijo: «¡Dispara!», y él disparó. Entonces Eliseo dijo: «¡Es la flecha de la victoria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, la flecha de la victoria sobre Aram! Derrotarás a Aram en Afec hasta acabar con él».
es.R: «Abre la ventana del lado oriental», le dijo Eliseo, y el rey la abrió. «¡Dispara!», le dijo Eliseo, y el rey disparó. Entonces Eliseo dijo: «¡Esta es la flecha de la victoria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, la flecha que significa victoria sobre Aram! Vencerás a los arameos en Afec hasta exterminarlos».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Ouvre la fenêtre vers l’orient. » Et il [l’]ouvrit. Et Élisée dit : « Tire. » Et il tira. Et il dit : « Flèche de victoire pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et flèche de victoire contre Aram ! Et tu frapperas Aram à Aphek jusqu’à l’achever. »
fr.B: Il dit : « Ouvre la fenêtre du côté de l’orient », et le roi l’ouvrit. Élisée dit : « Tire ! », et il tira. Élisée dit alors : « Flèche de victoire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, flèche de victoire contre Aram ! Tu battras Aram à Aphek jusqu’à l’anéantir. »
fr.R: « Ouvre la fenêtre qui donne à l’est », a dit Élisée, et le roi l’a ouverte. « Tire ! » a dit Élisée, et le roi a tiré. Alors Élisée a dit : « C’est la flèche de la victoire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, la flèche qui annonce la victoire sur Aram ! Tu battras les Araméens à Aphek jusqu’à les détruire complètement. »

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Fungua dirisha upande wa mashariki." Naye akalifungua. Naye Elisha akasema, "Piga mshale." Naye akapiga. Naye akasema, "Mshale wa ushindi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na mshale wa ushindi juu ya Aramu! Nawe utaipiga Aramu huko Afeki mpaka kuikomesha."
sw.B: Akasema, "Fungua dirisha linaloelekea mashariki," naye akalifungua. Elisha akasema, "Piga mshale!" naye akapiga. Kisha Elisha akasema, "Mshale wa ushindi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mshale wa ushindi juu ya Aramu! Utaishinda Aramu huko Afeki mpaka uimalize kabisa."
sw.R: "Fungua dirisha la upande wa mashariki," Elisha akasema, naye mfalme akalifungua. "Piga mshale!" Elisha akasema, naye mfalme akapiga. Kisha Elisha akasema, "Huu ni mshale wa ushindi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mshale unaoonyesha ushindi juu ya Aramu! Utawashinda Waaramu huko Afeki mpaka uwaangamize kabisa."

vi.L: Ông nói: "Hãy mở cửa sổ về phía đông." Vua mở [ra]. Ê-li-sê nói: "Hãy bắn." Vua bắn. Ông nói: "Mũi tên chiến thắng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, mũi tên chiến thắng trên A-ram! Vua sẽ đánh A-ram tại A-phéc cho đến khi tiêu diệt hết."
vi.B: Ông nói: "Xin mở cửa sổ phía đông," và vua mở ra. Ê-li-sê nói: "Bắn đi!" và vua bắn. Ê-li-sê nói: "Đó là mũi tên chiến thắng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, mũi tên chiến thắng A-ram! Vua sẽ đánh bại A-ram tại A-phéc cho đến khi tiêu diệt chúng."
vi.R: "Xin vua mở cửa sổ phía đông," Ê-li-sê nói, và vua mở ra. "Bắn đi!" Ê-li-sê nói, và vua bắn. Rồi Ê-li-sê nói: "Đây là mũi tên chiến thắng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, mũi tên báo hiệu chiến thắng trên A-ram! Vua sẽ đánh bại quân A-ram tại A-phéc cho đến khi tiêu diệt hết chúng."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "동쪽으로 [난] 창문을 여십시오." 그리고 그가 [그것을] 열었다. 그리고 엘리사가 말했다. "쏘십시오." 그리고 그가 쏘았다. 그리고 그가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 승리의 화살, 곧 아람에 대한 승리의 화살입니다! 당신은 아벡에서 아람을 쳐서 끝장을 낼 것입니다."
ko.B: 엘리사가 "동쪽 창문을 여십시오" 하고 말하자, 왕이 창문을 열었다. 엘리사가 "쏘십시오!" 하자, 왕이 쏘았다. 그러자 엘리사가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 승리의 화살, 아람을 이기는 승리의 화살입니다! 임금님께서는 아벡에서 아람을 쳐서 끝장내실 것입니다."
ko.R: "동쪽 창문을 여십시오." 엘리사가 말하자 왕이 창문을 열었다. "쏘십시오!" 엘리사가 말하자 왕이 활을 쏘았다. 그러자 엘리사가 말했다. "이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주시는 승리의 화살, 아람 사람들을 이긴다는 뜻의 화살입니다! 임금님께서는 아벡에서 아람 사람들을 쳐서 완전히 없애실 것입니다."

decisions.choice: victory: rescue won by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "deliverer" in verse 5. It is used of the rescue Yahweh gives in battle (1 Samuel 11:13; 19:5). The arrow belongs to Yahweh: the victory will be his.

decisions.choice: eastward ... Aphek: toward Aram
decisions.reason: Aram lay to the north and east of Israel. Aphek was probably the town east of the Sea of Galilee where Ahab had defeated an earlier Ben-hadad (1 Kings 20:26-30).

decisions.choice: you will strike Aram ... until making an end: a promise of complete victory
decisions.reason: The promise is full, but how much of it the king receives depends on what he does next (verses 18-19).

decisions.choice: the LORD's victory; strike down / defeat; Aram / the Arameans
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "for the LORD" into the possessive. Readable names the people, "the Arameans", for the nation "Aram", and says "wiped them out" for "made an end".

decisions.choice: speaker named after the words
decisions.reason: Readable names Elisha and the king in each short exchange so that it is clear who speaks and who acts.

decisions.choice: "Derrotarás a Aram" (B); "Vencerás a los arameos" (R); "Afec"
decisions.reason: Readable names the people, "los arameos", as the English does; "Afec" is the usual Spanish form of Aphek.

decisions.choice: "battras"; "Aram" (B), "les Araméens" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "battre" for "strike" in war, as the English says "strike down" and "defeat"; Readable names the people, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Waaramu
decisions.reason: Readable names the people, as the English does with "the Arameans"; Literal and Balanced keep the name of the land, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: "임금님께서는 ... 끝장내실 것입니다" when Elisha speaks of the king's future
decisions.reason: In a promise about the king himself, Balanced and Readable name him "임금님" with the honorific, the natural courtesy of Korean; Literal keeps "당신".

source.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר קַ֥ח הַחִצִּ֖ים וַיִּקָּ֑ח וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לְמֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַךְ־אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּ֥ךְ שָֽׁלֹשׁ־פְּעָמִ֖ים וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Take the arrows; and he took. And he said to [the] king of Israel, Strike [the] ground; and he struck three times and stopped.

en.L: And he said, "Take the arrows." And he took [them]. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike [the] ground." And he struck three times and stopped.
en.B: "Take the arrows," he said, and the king took them. Then he told the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." He struck it three times and stopped.
en.R: Then Elisha said, "Pick up the arrows." The king picked them up. Elisha told him, "Strike the ground with them." The king struck the ground three times and then stopped.

es.L: Y dijo: «Toma las flechas». Y [las] tomó. Y dijo al rey de Israel: «Golpea [el] suelo». Y golpeó tres veces, y se detuvo.
es.B: «Toma las flechas», le dijo, y el rey las tomó. Luego le dijo al rey de Israel: «Golpea el suelo». Él lo golpeó tres veces y se detuvo.
es.R: Luego Eliseo le dijo: «Toma las flechas». El rey las tomó. Eliseo le dijo: «Golpea el suelo con ellas». El rey golpeó el suelo tres veces y luego se detuvo.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Prends les flèches. » Et il [les] prit. Et il dit au roi d’Israël : « Frappe [le] sol. » Et il frappa trois fois, et il s’arrêta.
fr.B: « Prends les flèches », dit-il, et le roi les prit. Puis il dit au roi d’Israël : « Frappe le sol. » Il frappa trois fois et s’arrêta.
fr.R: Ensuite Élisée a dit : « Prends les flèches. » Le roi les a prises. Élisée lui a dit : « Frappe le sol avec. » Le roi a frappé le sol trois fois, puis il s’est arrêté.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Chukua mishale." Naye akaichukua. Naye akamwambia mfalme wa Israeli, "Piga [chini] ardhi." Naye akapiga mara tatu, akaacha.
sw.B: Akasema, "Chukua mishale," naye mfalme akaichukua. Kisha akamwambia mfalme wa Israeli, "Piga ardhi." Akaipiga mara tatu, akaacha.
sw.R: Kisha Elisha akasema, "Iokote mishale." Mfalme akaiokota. Elisha akamwambia, "Piga ardhi kwa mishale hiyo." Mfalme akapiga ardhi mara tatu, kisha akaacha.

vi.L: Ông nói: "Hãy lấy các mũi tên." Vua lấy [chúng]. Ông nói với vua Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Hãy đập xuống đất." Vua đập ba lần rồi ngừng.
vi.B: "Xin vua lấy các mũi tên," ông nói, và vua lấy. Rồi ông bảo vua Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Xin vua đập xuống đất." Vua đập ba lần rồi ngừng.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-li-sê nói: "Xin vua cầm các mũi tên lên." Vua cầm lên. Ê-li-sê bảo vua: "Xin vua dùng chúng đập xuống đất." Vua đập xuống đất ba lần rồi ngừng.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "화살들을 가지십시오." 그리고 그가 [그것들을] 가졌다. 그리고 그가 이스라엘 왕에게 말했다. "땅을 치십시오." 그리고 그가 세 번 치고 멈추었다.
ko.B: 엘리사가 "화살을 집으십시오" 하고 말하자, 왕이 화살을 집었다. 엘리사가 이스라엘 왕에게 "땅을 치십시오" 하고 말하자, 왕은 땅을 세 번 치고 멈추었다.
ko.R: 엘리사가 말했다. "화살들을 집으십시오." 왕이 화살들을 집었다. 엘리사가 왕에게 말했다. "그 화살들로 땅을 치십시오." 왕은 땅을 세 번 치고 나서 멈추었다.

decisions.choice: strike the ground: beat the ground with the arrows
alternatives: shoot the arrows into the ground
decisions.reason: The king most likely struck the ground with the bundle of arrows. The words could also mean shooting arrows into the ground. Either way the verb is the one used for striking down Aram (verses 17, 19), so each blow stands for a victory.

decisions.choice: stopped: held back
decisions.reason: The king stopped of his own accord after three blows; Elisha had set no number (verse 19).

decisions.choice: with them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the king struck the ground with (m1).

source.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֨ף עָלָ֜יו אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְהַכּ֨וֹת חָמֵ֤שׁ אוֹ־שֵׁשׁ֙ פְּעָמִ֔ים אָ֛ז הִכִּ֥יתָ אֶת־אֲרָ֖ם עַד־כַּלֵּ֑ה וְעַתָּ֕ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים תַּכֶּ֥ה אֶת־אֲרָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And was angry with him [the] man of the God and said, To strike five or six times! Then you would have struck Aram until finishing; and now three times you will strike Aram.

en.L: And the man of God was angry with him and said, "[You ought] to strike five or six times! Then you would have struck Aram until making an end. But now three times you will strike Aram."
en.B: The man of God was angry with him. "You ought to have struck five or six times!" he said. "Then you would have struck Aram down until it was finished. As it is, you will strike Aram down only three times."
en.R: The man of God was angry with him. "You should have hit the ground five or six times!" he said. "Then you would have defeated Aram completely. But now you will defeat Aram only three times."

es.L: Y el hombre de Dios se enojó con él y dijo: «¡[Debías] golpear cinco o seis veces! Entonces habrías herido a Aram hasta acabar. Pero ahora tres veces herirás a Aram».
es.B: El hombre de Dios se enojó con él. «¡Tenías que haber golpeado cinco o seis veces!», le dijo. «Entonces habrías derrotado a Aram hasta acabar con él. Pero ahora derrotarás a Aram solo tres veces».
es.R: El hombre de Dios se enojó con él. «¡Debiste golpear el suelo cinco o seis veces!», le dijo. «Así habrías vencido a Aram por completo. Pero ahora vencerás a Aram solo tres veces».

fr.L: Et l’homme de Dieu s’irrita contre lui et dit : « [Il fallait] frapper cinq ou six fois ! Alors tu aurais frappé Aram jusqu’à l’achever. Mais maintenant tu frapperas Aram trois fois. »
fr.B: L’homme de Dieu se mit en colère contre lui. « Il fallait frapper cinq ou six fois ! dit-il. Alors tu aurais battu Aram jusqu’à l’anéantir. Maintenant, tu ne battras Aram que trois fois. »
fr.R: L’homme de Dieu s’est fâché contre lui. « Tu aurais dû frapper le sol cinq ou six fois ! a-t-il dit. Alors tu aurais vaincu Aram complètement. Mais maintenant, tu ne vaincras Aram que trois fois. »

sw.L: Naye mtu wa Mungu akamkasirikia, akasema, "[Ungepaswa] kupiga mara tano au sita! Ndipo ungeipiga Aramu mpaka kuikomesha. Lakini sasa utaipiga Aramu mara tatu."
sw.B: Mtu wa Mungu akamkasirikia. Akasema, "Ungepaswa kupiga mara tano au sita! Ndipo ungeishinda Aramu mpaka ikakoma kabisa. Lakini sasa utaishinda Aramu mara tatu tu."
sw.R: Mtu wa Mungu alimkasirikia. Akasema, "Ungepaswa kupiga ardhi mara tano au sita! Ndipo ungeishinda Aramu kabisa. Lakini sasa utaishinda Aramu mara tatu tu."

vi.L: Người của Đức Chúa Trời nổi giận với vua mà nói: "[Lẽ ra vua phải] đập năm hay sáu lần! Bấy giờ vua sẽ đánh A-ram cho đến khi tiêu diệt hết. Nhưng nay vua sẽ đánh A-ram ba lần."
vi.B: Người của Đức Chúa Trời nổi giận với vua. Ông nói: "Lẽ ra vua phải đập năm hay sáu lần! Như thế vua sẽ đánh bại A-ram cho đến khi chúng bị tiêu diệt. Còn bây giờ vua sẽ chỉ đánh bại A-ram ba lần thôi."
vi.R: Người của Đức Chúa Trời nổi giận với vua. Ông nói: "Lẽ ra vua phải đập xuống đất năm hay sáu lần! Như thế vua đã đánh bại A-ram hoàn toàn. Nhưng bây giờ vua sẽ chỉ thắng A-ram ba lần mà thôi."

ko.L: 그리고 하나님의 사람이 그에게 화를 내며 말했다. "다섯 번이나 여섯 번 쳤어야 [했습니다]! 그러면 당신이 아람을 쳐서 끝장을 냈을 것입니다. 그러나 이제 당신은 세 번 아람을 칠 것입니다."
ko.B: 하나님의 사람이 그에게 화를 내며 말했다. "다섯 번이나 여섯 번은 치셨어야 했습니다! 그러면 아람을 쳐서 완전히 끝장내셨을 것입니다. 그러나 이제는 아람을 세 번만 치실 것입니다."
ko.R: 하나님의 사람 엘리사가 왕에게 화를 내며 말했다. "땅을 다섯 번이나 여섯 번은 치셨어야 했습니다! 그랬다면 아람을 완전히 이기셨을 것입니다. 그러나 이제는 아람을 세 번만 이기실 것입니다."

decisions.choice: to strike five or six times: you should have struck
decisions.reason: The bare verb form states what ought to have been done.

decisions.choice: the king's half-hearted act limits the victory
decisions.reason: The sign was Yahweh's promise put into the king's hands. By stopping at three he showed how little he expected, and he receives what he acted out: three victories (verse 25), not the full end of Aram's power.

decisions.choice: the man of God: the prophet Elisha
decisions.reason: The usual title for Elisha in Kings (4:7; 8:2).

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "only", which the contrast with "five or six times" implies.

decisions.choice: strike ... down
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "strike" for the blows on the ground and "strike down" for Aram, so the link between the sign and the battles stays visible. Readable says "defeat".

source.text: וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִישָׁ֖ע וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֑הוּ וּגְדוּדֵ֥י מוֹאָ֛ב יָבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ בָּ֥א שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Elisha and they buried him; and bands of Moab would come into [the] land [at the] coming of [the] year.

en.L: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And bands of Moab would come into the land at the coming of the year.
en.B: Elisha died, and they buried him. Now raiding bands from Moab used to come into the land each spring.
en.R: Then Elisha died and was buried. Groups of raiders from Moab used to invade the land every spring.

es.L: Y murió Eliseo, y lo sepultaron. Y bandas de Moab entraban en la tierra al venir el año.
es.B: Eliseo murió y lo sepultaron. En aquel tiempo, bandas de saqueadores de Moab solían invadir la tierra cada primavera.
es.R: Después Eliseo murió y fue sepultado. Grupos de saqueadores de Moab solían invadir el país cada primavera.

fr.L: Et Élisée mourut, et on l’enterra. Et des bandes de Moab venaient dans le pays à l’arrivée de l’année.
fr.B: Élisée mourut, et on l’enterra. Or des bandes de pillards moabites envahissaient le pays chaque printemps.
fr.R: Puis Élisée est mort et on l’a enterré. Chaque printemps, des groupes de pillards venus de Moab envahissaient le pays.

sw.L: Naye Elisha akafa, wakamzika. Na vikosi vya Moabu vilikuwa vikiingia katika nchi wakati wa kuingia kwa mwaka.
sw.B: Elisha alikufa, wakamzika. Basi vikosi vya wavamizi kutoka Moabu vilikuwa vikiingia katika nchi kila majira ya kuchipua.
sw.R: Kisha Elisha akafa, akazikwa. Makundi ya wavamizi kutoka Moabu yalikuwa yakiivamia nchi kila mwaka wakati wa masika.

vi.L: Ê-li-sê qua đời và người ta chôn ông. Các toán [quân] Mô-áp thường đến xâm nhập xứ vào lúc đầu năm.
vi.B: Ê-li-sê qua đời và người ta chôn ông. Bấy giờ các toán quân cướp từ Mô-áp thường kéo vào xứ mỗi mùa xuân.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-li-sê qua đời và được chôn cất. Các toán quân cướp từ Mô-áp thường kéo vào đánh phá xứ mỗi mùa xuân.

ko.L: 그리고 엘리사가 죽었고, 사람들이 그를 묻었다. 그리고 모압의 무리들이 해가 바뀔 때에 그 땅에 들어오곤 했다.
ko.B: 엘리사가 죽자 사람들이 그를 묻었다. 그 무렵 모압의 약탈자 무리가 해마다 봄이 되면 그 땅에 쳐들어오곤 했다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 엘리사가 죽어서 묻혔다. 그 무렵 모압의 도적 떼가 해마다 봄이 되면 이스라엘 땅에 쳐들어오곤 했다.

decisions.choice: bands: raiding parties
decisions.reason: The word means small armed groups that raid for plunder rather than a full army (5:2; 6:23).

decisions.choice: at the coming of the year: in spring
decisions.reason: The year was counted from the spring, and spring was the season when kings went out to war (2 Samuel 11:1; 1 Kings 20:22, 26). The words could also be read as "year after year" or "in that year".

decisions.choice: would come: a repeated event
decisions.reason: The verb describes what used to happen, which sets the scene for verse 21.

decisions.choice: was buried
decisions.reason: Readable uses the passive, as in the death formula, since the Hebrew does not say who buried him.

decisions.choice: "cada primavera"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the season meant, as the English does (m2); Literal keeps "al venir el año".

decisions.choice: imperfect "envahissaient"
decisions.reason: The raids were repeated (m3); French uses the imparfait for repeated action at every level, Readable included.

decisions.choice: kila majira ya kuchipua (Balanced); kila mwaka wakati wa masika (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The coming of the year" is spring, after the winter rains (meaning decision m2). Readable uses "masika", the familiar season of rains, as the nearest everyday word; a reviewer may prefer another.

records.literal_gloss: And it was, they [were] burying a man, and look, they saw the band, and they threw the man into [the] grave of Elisha; and went and touched the man [the] bones of Elisha, and he lived and stood on his feet.

en.L: And it happened [as] they were burying a man, and look, they saw the band, and they threw the man into the grave of Elisha. And the man went and touched the bones of Elisha, and he lived and stood up on his feet.
en.B: Once, as some people were burying a man, suddenly they saw a raiding band, and they threw the man into Elisha's grave. When the man touched Elisha's bones, he came to life and stood up on his feet.
en.R: One time some people were burying a man, and suddenly they saw a band of raiders. So they threw the body into Elisha's grave. When the dead man touched Elisha's bones, he came back to life and stood up on his feet.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras sepultaban a un hombre, he aquí que vieron la banda, y arrojaron al hombre en la tumba de Eliseo; y el hombre fue y tocó los huesos de Eliseo, y revivió y se levantó sobre sus pies.
es.B: Una vez, mientras unos estaban sepultando a un hombre, de pronto vieron una banda de saqueadores, y arrojaron al hombre en la tumba de Eliseo. Cuando el hombre tocó los huesos de Eliseo, revivió y se puso de pie.
es.R: Una vez, unas personas estaban sepultando a un hombre, y de repente vieron una banda de saqueadores. Entonces echaron el cuerpo en la tumba de Eliseo. Cuando el muerto tocó los huesos de Eliseo, volvió a la vida y se puso de pie.

fr.L: Et il arriva [qu’]ils enterraient un homme, et voici, ils virent la bande, et ils jetèrent l’homme dans le tombeau d’Élisée. Et l’homme alla toucher les os d’Élisée, et il reprit vie et se leva sur ses pieds.
fr.B: Un jour, alors qu’on enterrait un homme, on aperçut soudain une de ces bandes, et l’on jeta l’homme dans le tombeau d’Élisée. Dès que l’homme toucha les os d’Élisée, il reprit vie et se dressa sur ses pieds.
fr.R: Un jour, des gens étaient en train d’enterrer un homme. Tout à coup, ils ont vu arriver une bande de pillards. Alors ils ont jeté le corps dans le tombeau d’Élisée. Quand le mort a touché les os d’Élisée, il est revenu à la vie et s’est mis debout.

sw.L: Ikawa walipokuwa wakimzika mtu, na tazama, wakakiona kikosi, wakamtupa mtu huyo ndani ya kaburi la Elisha. Naye mtu huyo akaenda na kuigusa mifupa ya Elisha, akaishi, akasimama kwa miguu yake.
sw.B: Wakati mmoja watu walipokuwa wakimzika mtu, ghafla wakaona kikosi cha wavamizi, wakamtupa mtu huyo ndani ya kaburi la Elisha. Mtu huyo alipoigusa mifupa ya Elisha, akawa hai, akasimama kwa miguu yake.
sw.R: Siku moja watu walikuwa wakimzika mtu, na ghafla wakaona kundi la wavamizi. Kwa hiyo wakautupa mwili ndani ya kaburi la Elisha. Yule maiti alipoigusa mifupa ya Elisha, akafufuka, akasimama kwa miguu yake.

vi.L: Xảy ra, [khi] người ta đang chôn một người, kìa, họ thấy toán quân, và họ ném người ấy vào mộ của Ê-li-sê. Người ấy đi xuống, chạm vào hài cốt Ê-li-sê, thì sống lại và đứng dậy trên chân mình.
vi.B: Có lần, khi người ta đang chôn một người, bỗng họ thấy một toán quân cướp, nên họ ném người ấy vào mộ Ê-li-sê. Khi người ấy chạm vào hài cốt Ê-li-sê, thì sống lại và đứng dậy trên chân mình.
vi.R: Có một lần, người ta đang chôn một người thì bỗng thấy một toán quân cướp. Họ liền ném xác người ấy vào mộ Ê-li-sê. Khi người chết chạm vào hài cốt Ê-li-sê, thì sống lại và đứng dậy được.

ko.L: 그리고 [그들이] 한 사람을 묻고 있을 때에, 보라, 그들이 그 무리를 보고 그 사람을 엘리사의 무덤에 던졌다. 그리고 그 사람이 내려가 엘리사의 뼈에 닿자, 그가 살아나서 자기 발로 일어섰다.
ko.B: 한번은 사람들이 어떤 사람을 묻고 있었는데, 갑자기 약탈자 무리가 보였다. 그래서 그들은 그 사람을 엘리사의 무덤에 던져 넣었다. 그 사람이 엘리사의 뼈에 닿자, 그는 살아나서 제 발로 일어섰다.
ko.R: 한번은 사람들이 죽은 사람을 묻고 있었는데, 갑자기 도적 떼가 나타났다. 그래서 그들은 그 시체를 엘리사의 무덤에 던져 넣었다. 죽은 사람이 엘리사의 뼈에 닿자, 그는 다시 살아나서 제 발로 일어섰다.

decisions.choice: went and touched: as soon as the body went down and touched
decisions.reason: The two verbs together describe the body coming to rest against Elisha's bones; the second action follows straight on the first.

decisions.choice: the grave: probably a tomb cut in rock
decisions.reason: Tombs were often caves or rooms cut in rock, closed by a stone, where bodies were laid on shelves. Such a tomb could be opened quickly, and the body could touch the bones of one buried earlier.

decisions.choice: he lived: Yahweh's power to give life, shown through his prophet even after his death
decisions.reason: Elisha had raised the Shunammite's son (4:32-37). Even in death the prophet is a sign that Yahweh is still at work for Israel, and that his word to Joash (verses 17-19) will not fail.

decisions.choice: Once / One time; suddenly
decisions.reason: "And it happened" opens a new episode; Balanced and Readable say "Once" or "One time". The word "look" marks a sudden sight and becomes "suddenly".

decisions.choice: the body; the dead man
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the man thrown into the grave was dead.

records.literal_gloss: And was gracious Yahweh to them and had compassion on them and turned to them for the sake of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and not he was willing to destroy them, and not he cast them from upon his face until now.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was gracious to them and had compassion on them and turned to them, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not willing to destroy them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not cast them from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence until now.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was gracious to them and had compassion on them. He turned toward them for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not yet cast them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was kind to them and had pity on them. He cared for them because of the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not yet send them away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

vi.R: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tử tế với họ và thương xót họ. Ngài chăm sóc họ vì giao ước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lập với Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Gia-cốp. Ngài không muốn tiêu diệt họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chưa đuổi họ đi khỏi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 은혜를 베푸시고 그들을 불쌍히 여기시고 그들에게로 향하셨다. 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱과 맺으신 그분의 언약 때문이었다. 그리고 그분께서는 그들을 멸하기를 원하지 않으셨고, 지금까지 그들을 그분의 얼굴 앞에서 던져 버리지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들에게 은혜를 베푸시고 그들을 불쌍히 여기셨다. 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱과 맺으신 언약 때문에 그들을 돌아보셨다. 그분께서는 그들을 멸하려 하지 않으셨고, 아직은 그들을 그분 앞에서 쫓아내지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들에게 친절을 베푸시고 그들을 가엾게 여기셨다. 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱과 맺으신 언약 때문에 그들을 보살피셨다. 그분께서는 그들을 멸망시키려 하지 않으셨고, 아직은 그들을 그분 앞에서 쫓아내지 않으셨다.

decisions.choice: was gracious ... had compassion ... turned to them: Yahweh's undeserved favor
decisions.reason: Three verbs build up the picture: Yahweh showed favor, felt the tender pity of a parent, and turned his face toward them in care. None of it was earned; the kings of these years did evil (verses 2, 11).

decisions.choice: his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: the promises to Israel's ancestors
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised the land and a people to Abraham and confirmed it to Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 15:18; 26:3-5; 28:13-15). In Egypt he remembered this covenant (Exodus 2:24), and he promised to remember it even after Israel's sin (Leviticus 26:42). This is the only time Kings names the three ancestors together.

decisions.choice: cast them from his presence: send them into exile
decisions.reason: The same words describe the fall of Israel to Assyria and later of Judah to Babylon (17:18, 20, 23; 24:20).

decisions.choice: until now: as yet
alternatives: up to the writer's own day
decisions.reason: The phrase looks ahead: Yahweh held back the exile at this time, though it came later (17:6, 23). It is not a claim that Israel was still in the land when the book was written.

decisions.choice: But; had not yet / did not yet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the contrast with the oppression of verse 22, and turn "until now" into "not yet" (m4).

decisions.choice: kind ... had pity ... cared for them
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the three verbs, and says "the covenant he had made".

decisions.choice: "todavía no"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "until now" into "not yet", as the English does (m4); Literal keeps "hasta ahora".

decisions.choice: "ne les avait pas encore rejetés" (B); "ne les a pas encore chassés" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, "until now" becomes "not yet" at Balanced and Readable, which lets the reader feel the coming exile (m4).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for God in narration
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has a free pronoun for God, "Ngài", which takes the deity_pronoun span mid-sentence and is written plainly with its capital at the start of a sentence, as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: Ben-hadad his son: a later king of that name
decisions.reason: Hazael had seized the throne of Aram by killing an earlier Ben-hadad (8:7-15). His son took that name, which earlier kings of Damascus had borne (1 Kings 15:18; 20:1).

source.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן־יְהוֹאָחָ֗ז וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הֶֽעָרִים֙ מִיַּד֙ בֶּן־הֲדַ֣ד בֶּן־חֲזָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקַ֗ח מִיַּ֛ד יְהוֹאָחָ֥ז אָבִ֖יו בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הִכָּ֣הוּ יוֹאָ֔שׁ וַיָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־עָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And returned Jehoash son of Jehoahaz and took the cities from [the] hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael which he had taken from [the] hand of Jehoahaz his father in the war; three times struck him Joash, and he brought back [the] cities of Israel.

en.L: And Jehoash son of Jehoahaz again took the cities from [the] hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, which he had taken from [the] hand of Jehoahaz his father in the war. Three times Joash struck him, and he brought back the cities of Israel.
en.B: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz recaptured from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that Ben-hadad had taken in war from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash struck him down, and he recovered the cities of Israel.
en.R: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz won back the towns that Ben-hadad son of Hazael had captured in war from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash defeated Ben-hadad, and he got back the towns of Israel.

es.L: Y Joás hijo de Joacaz volvió a tomar de mano de Ben-adad hijo de Hazael las ciudades que este había tomado de mano de Joacaz su padre en la guerra. Tres veces lo hirió Joás, y recuperó las ciudades de Israel.
es.B: Entonces Joás hijo de Joacaz reconquistó de manos de Ben-adad hijo de Hazael las ciudades que Ben-adad le había quitado en la guerra a su padre Joacaz. Tres veces lo derrotó Joás, y recobró las ciudades de Israel.
es.R: Entonces Joás hijo de Joacaz recuperó las ciudades que Ben-adad hijo de Hazael le había quitado en la guerra a su padre Joacaz. Tres veces venció Joás a Ben-adad, y así recuperó las ciudades de Israel.

fr.L: Et Yehoash fils de Joachaz reprit des mains de Ben-Hadad fils de Hazaël les villes qu’il avait prises des mains de Joachaz son père dans la guerre. Trois fois Joas le frappa, et il recouvra les villes d’Israël.
fr.B: Alors Yehoash, fils de Joachaz, reprit à Ben-Hadad, fils de Hazaël, les villes que celui-ci avait prises par les armes à son père Joachaz. Trois fois Joas le battit, et il recouvra les villes d’Israël.
fr.R: Alors Yehoash fils de Joachaz a repris les villes que Ben-Hadad fils de Hazaël avait conquises pendant la guerre contre son père Joachaz. Trois fois, Joas a vaincu Ben-Hadad, et il a récupéré les villes d’Israël.

sw.L: Naye Yehoashi mwana wa Yehoahazi akarudi akaitwaa miji kutoka mkononi mwa Ben-hadadi mwana wa Hazaeli, ambayo alikuwa ameitwaa kutoka mkononi mwa Yehoahazi baba yake katika vita. Mara tatu Yoashi alimpiga, naye akairudisha miji ya Israeli.
sw.B: Kisha Yehoashi mwana wa Yehoahazi akaiteka tena kutoka kwa Ben-hadadi mwana wa Hazaeli miji ambayo Ben-hadadi alikuwa ameitwaa vitani kutoka kwa Yehoahazi baba yake. Mara tatu Yoashi alimshinda, naye akairudisha miji ya Israeli.
sw.R: Kisha Yehoashi mwana wa Yehoahazi akairudisha miji ambayo Ben-hadadi mwana wa Hazaeli alikuwa ameiteka vitani kutoka kwa baba yake Yehoahazi. Mara tatu Yoashi alimshinda Ben-hadadi, naye akapata tena miji ya Israeli.

vi.L: Giê-hô-ách con trai Giô-a-cha lấy lại các thành từ tay Bên-Ha-đát con trai Ha-xa-ên, là các thành mà ông ấy đã lấy từ tay Giô-a-cha cha vua trong chiến tranh. Giô-ách đánh ông ấy ba lần, và thu hồi các thành của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Giê-hô-ách con trai Giô-a-cha chiếm lại từ tay Bên-Ha-đát con trai Ha-xa-ên các thành mà Bên-Ha-đát đã chiếm của Giô-a-cha cha vua trong chiến tranh. Giô-ách đánh bại Bên-Ha-đát ba lần và thu hồi các thành của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Rồi Giê-hô-ách con trai Giô-a-cha giành lại các thành mà Bên-Ha-đát con trai Ha-xa-ên đã chiếm của Giô-a-cha cha vua trong chiến tranh. Giô-ách thắng Bên-Ha-đát ba lần và lấy lại các thành của Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 여호아하스의 아들 여호아스가 하사엘의 아들 벤하닷의 손에서 성읍들을 다시 빼앗았다. 그것들은 그가 전쟁 중에 그의 아버지 여호아하스의 손에서 빼앗았던 것이었다. 요아스가 그를 세 번 쳐서 이스라엘의 성읍들을 되찾았다.
ko.B: 그리고 여호아하스의 아들 여호아스는, 하사엘의 아들 벤하닷이 전쟁으로 자기 아버지 여호아하스에게서 빼앗아 갔던 성읍들을 벤하닷에게서 도로 빼앗았다. 요아스는 그를 세 번 쳐부수고 이스라엘의 성읍들을 되찾았다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 여호아하스의 아들 여호아스는 하사엘의 아들 벤하닷이 전쟁으로 자기 아버지 여호아하스에게서 빼앗아 갔던 성읍들을 다시 찾아왔다. 요아스는 벤하닷을 세 번 물리치고 이스라엘의 성읍들을 되찾았다.

decisions.choice: returned and took: took back
decisions.reason: "Returned" with a second verb means doing something again, here taking back what had been lost.

decisions.choice: which he had taken from Jehoahaz: Ben-hadad had captured them in Jehoahaz's reign
decisions.reason: Ben-hadad seems to have led Aram's wars while his father Hazael was still king (verse 3). The cities Hazael took east of the Jordan in Jehu's day (10:32-33) are not said to be won back here; that came later under Jeroboam (14:25).

decisions.choice: three times Joash struck him: Elisha's word fulfilled
decisions.reason: The three victories are exactly what Elisha said after the king struck the ground three times (verse 19).

decisions.choice: Jehoash ... Joash: the same king
decisions.reason: The verse uses both forms of the name (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: struck him down / defeated; recovered / got back
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "strike" so the fulfillment of verse 19 is heard; Readable says "defeated", as there. Readable says "towns", the more usual word for places of this size.

decisions.choice: "lo derrotó" (B); "venció" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the verbs of Elisha's words in verse 19, "derrotarás" and "vencerás", so the fulfilment is heard.

decisions.choice: akarudi akaitwaa
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pair of verbs, "returned and took"; Swahili reads it, as Hebrew does, as "took back".
